hedge_fund/llm/client.py:290.loses: deepseek-flash now resolves, on Router-bound requests only, to Router's catalog id deepseek-v4.1-flash (same DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model, Router's spelling of it). The original request to DeepSeek is untouched on fallback, so DeepSeek's own API still sees 'deepseek-flash' if Router can't take the request.
hedge_fund/llm/client.py:290.why: ChatDeepSeek/langchain-deepseek builds its own openai.OpenAI client pointed at api.deepseek.com (an OpenAI-compatible host); Router's catalog carries this exact model family under a different id (deepseek-v4.1-flash, with several DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash spellings already aliased to it), so api.deepseek.com was unlocked and the app's id mapped to Router's. Implemented by hand (router-migrate's wrap/adapt codemods don't recognize langchain-deepseek's constructor or inject unlock_hosts into a langchain call), using router_runtime.wrap_openai(..., unlock_hosts=[...]) directly on every SDK client langchain_deepseek builds (ChatDeepSeek keeps a second, separate OpenAI client under '.client' besides '.root_client' — both needed unlocking). Verified end-to-end with `check --run`: a deepseek-flash call now reaches the Router simulator as a valid /v1/responses request.
